chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Abdullah, from Ali ibn Mansur, from Ismail Al-Jawzi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever comforts one who is grieving, will be clothed on the Day of Standing (Resurrection) with a garment of honor that will be loved for it.'

key_terms.الْمَوْقِفِ: the standing (on the Day of Judgment)
key_terms.حُلَّةً: a garment of honor or dress

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for comforting someone in grief according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this chain to emphasize the social virtue of *ta'ziyah* (condolences) as a means of spiritual elevation. The promise of being 'clothed in a beloved garment' (*hullah*) on the Day of Judgment signifies divine honor and acceptance, linking the earthly act of empathy to eternal reward in Shia eschatology.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Hassan, from Al Hassan Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Abdullah, from Ali Bin Mansour, from Ismail Al Jowzy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who comforts someone in grief would be clothed during the pausing (Day of Judgement) with such a garment, he would be loved by it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn Hassa’n from al-Hassan ibn Al-Husayn from Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah from Ali ibn Mansur from Isma’il al-Jawziy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah has said, ‘
Whoever offers condolences to a sorrowful person will, on the Station for clearance of accounts, receive a dress that will be presented to him.’”
